required_fixes: Correct H(Y|Z) P(z) denominator in est_entropy_rate_cmi(): use smoothed P(z)=(count_z+alpha*n_a*n_y)/n_smoothed (with n_smoothed=n_total+alpha*n_z*n_a*n_y) instead of current unsmoothed P(z)=count_z/n_total. Current implementation (run_experiment.py:298-309) mixes smoothed P(z,y) with unsmoothed P(z), inflating H(Y|Z) bias and producing negative CMI at alpha>=0.5. Re-run alpha sweep with corrected estimator before declaring estimator-class closure; recomputation shows corrected estimator still yields FALSIFIED-IN-SETTING (no alpha achieves both C1 and C3) but via different failure mode (small positive CMI 0.12/0.05 <0.5 rather than negative CMI).

Clarify control identity mapping: spec.json positive_control and prereg C3 define deterministic SPA as positive control (CMI=2.0 bits, threshold >=0.5), but run_experiment.py C3 uses stochastic SPA K3 (k3_value_stochastic) for threshold and permutation test, while deterministic SPA is relegated to supplementary baseline B-ENTROPY-RATE-DEG. Align code threshold with frozen spec or explicitly amend spec to define C3 as stochastic sensitivity and B-DEG as deterministic construct validation.

Restore missing baselines B-PLUGIN-KL-ALPHA1 and B-PLUGIN-KL-ALPHA0: spec.json and prereg list replication of parent plug-in KL alpha=1.0 (expected K3~0.099, |null|~0.064) and alpha=0 (expected K3~1.377, |null|~0.924) for direct comparison. No baseline controls were computed in this packet; include them or explicitly mark as not executed with justification, to preserve comparison table auditability.

validity_findings.description: est_entropy_rate_cmi() computes H(Y|Z,A) with smoothed joint P(z,a,y)=(count+alpha)/n_smoothed and H(Y|Z) with mixed denominators: P(z,y) smoothed sum_a(count+alpha)/n_smoothed but P(z)=count_z/n_total unsmoothed (run_experiment.py:299 p_z = z_counts[z]/n_total; 302-305 p_zy smoothed). Correct smoothed P(z) = (count_z+alpha*n_a*n_y)/n_smoothed. For n_z~841/1438, n_a=4, n_y=12, n_total=5000, alpha=0.5 n_smoothed~25184, the mismatch is numerically ~1% on P(y|z) (see audit recomputation) but systematically biases H(Y|Z) downward by 0.12-0.30 bits vs corrected estimator, producing artifactual negative CMI (-0.07 at alpha0.5, -0.19 at alpha1.0). The report correctly identifies Laplace cell-count inflation as root cause (report.md: why entropy-rate fails) but does not identify this additional denominator inconsistency.

Null means corrected (K2 50-100 shuffles): 0.361/0.062/0.022 vs producer 0.240/0.200/0.275. Corrected estimator still yields no alpha achieving both |null|<0.1 and K3>=0.5 (alpha0.1 fails C1, alpha0.5/1.0 fail C3), so FALSIFIED-IN-SETTING verdict is robust to this bug. Fix required before generalizing negative claims about entropy-rate class.

Parent handoff do_not_assume notes this mismatch does not overturn tradeoff, and audit V1 confirms tradeoff robust, but the asymmetry means C1 and C3 are measured in different conditioning spaces, complicating joint decision interpretation. validity_findings.description: B-ENTROPY-RATE-DEG on deterministic SPA (I=0 by construction where H(Y|Z,A)=0) yields negative CMI at alpha0.5 (-0.073) and alpha1.0 (-0.199) with producer estimator, and small positive 0.133/0.051 with corrected estimator. Report.md correctly calls this a construct-validation failure at these smoothing levels. This confirms Laplace smoothing introduces bias even on deterministic control where signal should be ~log2(4) style, reinforcing that failures are estimator-intrinsic not data-intrinsic.

Null std 0.0021 (alpha0.1), 0.00038 (alpha0.5), 0.00015 (alpha1.0) across 500 within-session permutations shows tightly concentrated null away from zero (bias systematic, not random). Observed null means 0.240/0.200/0.275 are 112-1833 sigma from zero, confirming systematic bias. This is correctly interpreted as bias not variance. No leakage in shuffle: within-session action-label permutation preserves session structure and url_before/url_after pairing as specified.

No MEASUREMENT_INVALID triggers: C6 48/48 pairs verified, C7 2 non-empty buckets (5-9:343 strata, 10-19:37 strata), narrowly passing frozen thresholds (>=2 buckets, >=30% strata with >=5 records would be threatened but K3 has 841 strata for 5000 records ~5.9 avg, K2 1438 strata ~3.5 avg). Sparse regime explains inflated MLE null but does not invalidate measurement per frozen priority (FALSIFIED overrides MEASUREMENT_INVALID).

All measurements at N=5000 only (50 sessions x100 steps, seed=42). No N=50000 or learning-curve condition tested, so cannot distinguish asymptotic bias from finite-sample smoothing artifact. Parent exploratory suggests bias asymptotic, but this experiment provides no N-sweep evidence. Falsification bounded to N=5000.

claim_ceiling: FALSIFIED-IN-SETTING for entropy-rate CMI = H(Y|Z)-H(Y|Z,A) via Laplace-smoothed histogram (alpha in {0.1,0.5,1.0}) on the stochastic 12-state SPA (50% hash routing +50% uniform over 4 candidates per (state,action), CANDIDATES 12x4) at N=5000 (50 sessions x100 steps, seed 42) with MIN_STRATUM_SIZE=5 and within-session shuffled-action null (500 permutations): no tested alpha achieves both |null_mean|<0.1 bits and K3>=0.5 bits. With producer (buggy) estimator all alphas fail C1 (0.24/0.20/0.27); with corrected P(z) estimator C1 passes at alpha0.5/1.0 but C3 fails (K3 0.12/0.05 <0.5), so joint C1+C3 still empty. Deterministic SPA construct validation also fails at alpha>=0.5 (negative CMI producer, 0.13/0.05 corrected <<0.5). Ceiling bounded to discrete Laplace-histogram entropy-rate on this SPA class, this N, this alpha set, this null framework. Does NOT close: Bayesian model comparison, likelihood-ratio, KSG/kNN/KDE or non-smoothed estimators, N=50000 or dense-strata regimes, continuous state representations, production Web transitions, or the 1.52-bit true CMI existence (MLE 1.377 bits, per-stratum PMI 1.46-1.69 bits remain established).

unresolved: Whether corrected entropy-rate estimator with alternative smoothing (Jeffreys alpha=0.5 with corrected P(z), Hellinger, or no smoothing) or with bias correction (e.g., Miller-Madow) achieves joint C1+C3 at some alpha not in {0.1,0.5,1.0} or at larger N (50000) where cell-count smoothing penalty is smaller relative to signal.

Whether global entropy-rate without Laplace smoothing (alpha=0 MLE) would pass C3 (likely yes, ~1.3 bits) but with what null bias; MLE alpha=0 not tested in this packet and would likely fail C1 by larger margin as in parent (parent alpha0 |null|=0.924).

Whether the consistent positive K3-K2 differences (0.192/0.112/0.082 producer; corrected similar) represent genuine beyond-Markov signal vs residual smoothing asymmetry between K2 (n_z 1438) and K3 (n_z 841) cell counts.

Whether Bayesian model comparison (Bayes factor action-dependent vs independent transition model) or likelihood-ratio tests bypass the Laplace cell-count bias entirely, as suggested by handoff next_question.

Generalization beyond 12-state hash SPA to production Web with continuous embeddings, larger vocabularies, or natural stochastic mixing: bias scales with n_z*n_a*n_y relative to N, so larger discrete spaces would worsen tradeoff.
Whether per-(state,action) PMI (1.46-1.69 bits, p=0.0, noted in handoff unknown) can serve as alternative detection paradigm without CMI aggregation, avoiding global smoothing penalty.
